title: Sudanese Anti-War Coalition Rejects Burhan-Backed 'National Dialogue,' Proposes Alternative Peace Roadmap
detail: A broad coalition of Sudanese anti-war political and civil forces — including the Somoud alliance led by former Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok, Abdel Wahid al-Nur's Sudan Liberation Movement, Mubarak al-Fadil's National Umma Party faction, and Wajedi Sleh's Baath Party — concluded a two-day consultative meeting in Addis Ababa on August 22-23, 2026 by formally rejecting the 'Sudanese-Sudanese dialogue' initiative that Sovereignty Council chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan had announced on August 14. The groups said the process, held under one warring party's protection, risked granting political legitimacy to military rule, legitimizing the status quo, and deepening Sudan's de facto division into rival zones of control. In place of Burhan's initiative, the coalition proposed an alternative three-track roadmap combining humanitarian assistance, a permanent ceasefire, and a civilian-led political process, insisting any peace process must involve independent parties and exclude the National Congress Party and Islamic Movement entirely.

media.caption: Sudanese anti-war political and civil forces, meeting in Addis Ababa, rejected Burhan's dialogue initiative and proposed an alternative peace roadmap on August 24, 2026.

title: US Adviser Boulos Proposes Sudan-Wide UN Arms Embargo Covering Drones at Security Council
detail: US Senior Advisor for Africa Massad Boulos presented a draft UN Security Council resolution on August 24, 2026 to expand Sudan's Darfur-only arms embargo (set to expire September 12, 2026) to cover the entire country and explicitly include drones, drone systems, and related technologies, citing OHCHR data that armed drones killed over 1,120 civilians in the first half of 2026 — roughly 80% of recorded civilian deaths in that period. Sudan rejected the proposal as equating the national army with the RSF paramilitary and undermining sovereignty; Russia and China, both veto-holding council members, opposed the expansion, with Russia calling Western sanctions 'economic strangulation.' France backed the US proposal and Denmark pledged $15.6 million in additional humanitarian aid. Sudanese army chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan dismissed the sanctions threat the same day at a Khartoum police graduation ceremony, vowing to continue fighting until 'every inch' of RSF-held territory is recaptured.
